correctness.rationale: Every Q-value is derived from a two-stage absorbing MDP. Solving the downstream odds recurrence gives p_k=p/(p+(1-p)ε^k); downstream values telescope in the upstream odds recursion, yielding exactly R_k=R_0(γ/r)^k[p+(1-p)ε^k]. The sign of the exact adjacent difference gives all parameter cases and the equality boundary; the integer threshold and explicit N-family are checked algebraically. A fractional-part decomposition gives K=log(1/p)/log(1/ε)+O(1) and min q_k=Θ(p^α), 0<α<1. Direct recurrence and closed form matched in 26,460 independent exact-rational grid cases and 744 exact-family steps. Proof covers all integers, not just tested cases.

value.rationale: The result isolates a mathematically significant delayed-credit phenomenon: an action with fixed strictly positive optimal Bellman advantage loses its probability for an arbitrarily prescribed number of exact improvement steps, while both state values strictly rise. The complete two-state classification, exact turn index and deep-trough exponent provide a quantitative limitation not visible in general asymptotic-value convergence. A two-stage chain is the smallest natural nontrivial setting where downstream policy evolution reverses upstream preference; the finding is not a fixed random slice or routine tabulated number. Applications to sampled policy learning are not claimed.
